result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the cognitive barrier of "othering"—the hardwired tribal instinct that allows human beings to divide the world into "us" and "them." 

If that specific glitch in human psychology were removed, nearly every major catastrophe of human history would dissolve with it. War, systemic oppression, resource hoarding, political radicalization, and needless cruelty largely stem from the inability to genuinely feel the consciousness of the person across the ideological, geographical, or cultural divide as having the exact same weight and validity as one's own. 

Without the impulse to demonize the unfamiliar, empathy wouldn't be a practiced virtue; it would be the default state of existence. Problems like climate change, poverty, and injustice wouldn't be fought over as zero-sum games; they would be solved collaboratively, simply because the suffering of any part of the whole would be instinctively recognized as the suffering of the whole.
